questions.question: The Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur built by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajaraja I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brihadeswara Temple **at **Tanjavur **was built by **Rajaraja I**.
 
• Rajaraja I was a prominent ruler of the Chola dynasty in South India.
 
• The temple, also known as **Peruvudaiyar Kovil**, is a Hindu temple dedicated to **Lord Shiva**.
 
• It is one of the largest temples in India and is an outstanding example of Tamil architecture during the Chola period.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **magnificent vimana** (tower) and **intricate sculptures**.
 
• It was completed in **1010 AD **and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, recognized for its historical and architectural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajaraja I** ruled from **985 AD to 1014 AD** and expanded the Chola Empire significantly during his reign.
 
• He is credited with establishing a strong administration and commissioning several architectural projects, including the Brihadeswara Temple.
 
• The temple's construction marked the height of Chola architectural and cultural achievements.
 
• Rajaraja I's reign is often considered a **golden period in South Indian history**, known for advancements in art, architecture, and literature.
 
• The temple's design and construction techniques continue to be studied and admired by historians and architects around the world.

questions.question: Which diseases result from a deficiency of Vitamin B due to its insufficient intake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beri Beri**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Beri Beri** is a disease caused by a** deficiency of Vitamin B1** (thiamine).
 
• This condition can affect the **cardiovascular system** (wet beriberi) or the **nervous system** (dry beriberi).
 
• Symptoms of beriberi include weakness, pain in the limbs, shortness of breath, and swollen feet or legs.
 
• Vitamin B1 is essential for **glucose metabolism**, and its deficiency can lead to serious health issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vitamin B1 is found in foods such as whole grains, legumes, nuts, and seeds.
 
• Thiamine supplements can be used to treat and prevent beriberi, especially in populations with a high risk of deficiency.
 
• Other diseases caused by Vitamin B deficiencies include **pellagra **(caused by niacin deficiency) and **pernicious anemia **(caused by vitamin B12 deficiency).
 
• A balanced diet rich in various nutrients is crucial for preventing vitamin deficiencies and maintaining overall health.

questions.question: What is the minimum voting age for the citizens of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The minimum voting age for the citizens of India is **18 years**.
 
• This age limit was established by the **61st Amendment Act of 1988**, which lowered the voting age from** 21 to 18 years**.
 
• The amendment aimed to provide greater participation of the youth in the electoral process of the country.
 
• It reflects the Indian government's recognition of the maturity and capability of younger citizens to contribute to the democratic process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The voting age was reduced by the 61st Amendment of the Constitution of India, which was enacted in **1988**.
 
• Before the amendment, the minimum voting age was 21 years as per the original Constitution adopted in 1950.
 
• This change was made to encourage more young people to participate in the democratic process and to ensure that the youth of the country have a say in how the country is governed.
 
• India is the world's largest democracy, and the inclusion of younger voters adds to the robustness and representativeness of the electoral process.

questions.question: 'Anandamath' is a famous ___________ novel which was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anandamath** is a famous **Bengali** novel written by **Bankim Chandra Chatterjee**.
 
• It was first published in **1882 **and has since been considered a cornerstone of Bengali literature.
 
• The novel is set in the backdrop of the **Sannyasi Rebellion **in the late 18th century and is known for its patriotic theme.
 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee is one of the most notable authors in Bengali literature and has made significant contributions to the Indian literary canon.
 
• The novel also includes the famous song "**Vande Mataram**," which later became a national song of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee was born on 27 June 1838 and is considered one of the greatest novelists in Indian literature.
 
• He was a key figure in the literary renaissance of Bengal and was one of the first to write in both Bengali and English.
 
• Besides "Anandamath," some of his other notable works include "**Durgeshnandini**," "**Kapalkundala**," and "**Krishnakanter Will**."
 
• His works often explored themes of nationalism, social reform, and the cultural heritage of Bengal.
 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee passed away on 8 April 1894, leaving behind a rich legacy of literary works that continue to inspire generations.

questions.question: The four Nattuvanars namely Ponaiyah, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnaiya, who are renowned as Tanjaore Bandhu shaped up the modern day ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__

__
 
• The four Nattuvanars namely **Ponaiyah, Vadivelu, Sivanandam, and Chinnaiya**, who are renowned as **Tanjaore Bandhu**, shaped up the modern-day **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• These four brothers were instrumental in codifying and systematizing the dance form, which has its origins in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the **oldest classical dance forms** in India, and it combines elements of music, rhythm, and expressive dance.
 
• The efforts of the Tanjaore Bandhu helped in preserving and promoting this dance form, ensuring its continued popularity and practice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bharatanatyam is characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork, along with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• It is traditionally performed by women, but men also perform this dance form.
 
• The dance is usually accompanied by **classical Carnatic music **and a **nattuvanar **(a person who conducts the performance).
 
• Bharatanatyam has a rich repertoire of compositions and is known for its storytelling aspect, depicting themes from Hindu mythology and scriptures.

questions.question: Why are intermediate goods NOT included in the calculation of national income?

options.text: Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.
Intermediate goods are not produced within the country's borders.
Including intermediate goods would decrease the value of national income.
Intermediate goods are not important for measuring economic activity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.** This is because intermediate goods are used in the production of final goods and services. Including them separately in national income calculations would mean counting them multiple times.
 
• National income aims to measure the** value of final goods and services** produced within a country. Intermediate goods are already accounted for in the value of these final goods.
 
• By excluding intermediate goods, economists ensure that national income reflects the true economic activity and avoids inflation of the GDP figures.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and other inputs used in the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• National income is a crucial indicator of a country's economic performance and is used for comparing economic activity over time and between different economies.
 
• It includes measures such as **Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), and Net National Product (NNP)**.
 
• The exclusion of intermediate goods helps in avoiding the overestimation of national income and provides a clear picture of a nation's economic output.
 
• Intermediate goods can be transformed into final goods, which are then sold to consumers or used in further production processes.

questions.question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021,India’s rank is ________ out of 109 countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**66th**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021**, India's rank is **66th out of 109 countries**.
 
• The MPI is a measure that takes into account various deprivations faced by individuals in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• This ranking reflects India's efforts and challenges in addressing multidimensional poverty across the nation.
 
• The index is developed by the Oxford Poverty & Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The MPI complements traditional income-based poverty measures by considering multiple dimensions of poverty.
 
• It uses ten indicators across three dimensions:** health, education, and standard of living**, to provide a more comprehensive view of poverty.
 
• India's performance in the MPI highlights areas where significant progress has been made, as well as areas needing further attention and policy intervention.
 
• The 2021 MPI report emphasizes the **importance of addressing inequalities** and ensuring that no one is left behind in the development process.
 
• Global rankings like the MPI are crucial for guiding policy decisions and allocating resources effectively to combat poverty.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a bank statement?

• It helps account holders to understand their spending habits, monitor for any unauthorized transactions, and manage their finances effectively.
 
• Bank statements typically include **deposits, withdrawals, checks paid, interest earned**, and any fees or charges incurred.
 
• Regularly reviewing bank statements can help in budgeting and financial planning.

• They are typically issued monthly, though some banks may offer quarterly or even daily statements.
 
• It is important to review your bank statement for any discrepancies and report them to the bank promptly.
 
• Some banks also provide categorized summaries of spending to help customers better understand their financial behavior.

questions.question: Identify the southernmost range of the Himalaya from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiwaliks Range**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shiwaliks Range** is the **southernmost range** of the Himalayas.
 
• Also known as the **Outer Himalayas**, the Shiwaliks extend across the northern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• These ranges are geologically younger than the other ranges of the Himalayas and are composed of unconsolidated sediments.
 
• The Shiwaliks lie between the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** in the south and the **Lesser Himalayas** in the north.
 
• The elevation of the Shiwaliks ranges from 600 to 1500 meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayas are divided into four parallel longitudinal mountain belts: the **Trans-Himalayan Range, Greater Himalayas, Lesser Himalayas,** and the **Shiwaliks Range**.
 
• The **Trans-Himalayan Range** lies north of the Greater Himalayas and includes the **Karakoram and Ladakh ranges**.
 
• The **Greater Himalayas**, also known as the **Himadri**, contain the highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga.
 
• The **Lesser Himalayas**, or the **Himachal Range**, are situated between the Greater Himalayas and the Shiwaliks.
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in influencing the climate of the Indian subcontinent by acting as a barrier to the cold winds from Central Asia.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct about the Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: To ensure the above mentioned employment and clean working environment for men, women and children.
Providing adequate means of livelihood for both men and women
Ensuring equal remuneration for equal work only for men
Reorganizing the economic system to prevent the concentration of wealth in a few hands

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ensuring equal remuneration for equal work only for men**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** aim to **create a welfare state **in India.
 
• They provide guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• These principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to **ensure social and economic democracy**.
 
• Directive Principles advocate for equal pay for equal work for both men and women. Hence option 3 is not correct.
 
• Other options like ensuring employment, providing adequate means of livelihood, and preventing the concentration of wealth are aligned with the principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution, covering **Articles 36-51**.
 
• They are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are **not enforceable by any court**, but the principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• These principles aim to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all institutions of national life.
 
• Examples of the Directive Principles include the provision for free legal aid, promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections, and separation of the judiciary from the executive.

questions.question: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier** is widely regarded as the **father of modern chemistry**.
 
• He was instrumental in the chemical revolution of the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature.
 
• Lavoisier's work laid the foundation for the **law of conservation of mass**, which states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• He also helped develop the modern system for naming chemical substances, which replaced the older, less systematic names.
 
• His contributions significantly advanced the field of chemistry and helped transition it from alchemy to a more empirical and systematic science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joseph Priestley** also **discovered oxygen** independently around the same time as Lavoisier, but did not recognize it as an element.

questions.question: Independence Day is celebrated every year in Pakistan on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 August**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **14 August** is celebrated as **Independence Day** every year in **Pakistan**.
 
• Independence Day commemorates the day when Pakistan gained **independence from British rule in 1947**.
 
• It is a national holiday in Pakistan, marked by flag-raising ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and patriotic displays.
 
• On this day, the national flag is hoisted on public and private buildings, and special prayers are offered for the prosperity and development of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pakistan was created as a result of the **Pakistan Movement led by the All-India Muslim League** under the leadership of **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**.
 
• The movement sought a separate nation for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of British India.
 
• The partition of India and Pakistan led to mass migrations and significant upheaval, impacting millions of lives.
 
• Independence Day is observed with great zeal and enthusiasm across Pakistan, highlighting the country's cultural heritage and national pride.
 
• In **Islamabad, the capital city**, the main celebrations are held at the Presidential and Parliament buildings, where the President and Prime Minister deliver speeches.

questions.question: The word ‘yorker’ is related to which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yorker** is a term used in the sport of **Cricket**.
 
• A yorker is a delivery that pitches at the batsman's feet, making it difficult to play.
 
• It is often used by bowlers to prevent the batsman from scoring runs and to attempt to dismiss the batsman.
 
• Yorkers are considered to be one of the most effective deliveries in cricket, especially in the death overs of limited-overs matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cricket** is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of** eleven players** on a **field**.
 
• The game is played with a cricket ball and bat, and the objective is to score runs by hitting the ball and running between the wickets.
 
• Cricket is popular in countries like India, Australia, England, South Africa, and many others.
 
• The game has different formats, including **Test cricket, One Day Internationals (ODIs), and Twenty20 (T20) matches**.
 
• Key skills in cricket include batting, bowling, and fielding.
